newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kohl backs Waigel, rules out reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl backs Waigel, rules out reshuffle.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl backed Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Sunday after members of his own party said Waigel should be moved from his post if his plans for a reform of the tax system fell short of expectations.
"The demand for a cabinet reshuffle is totally absurd," Kohl told the Bild newspaper in an article released ahead of publication on Monday.
"Theo Waigel is a successful and internationally regarded finance minister, who has a difficult task to accomplish at the moment and has my full support," the chancellor said.
Some officials in Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) expressed doubts over the weekend about the work of Waigel's tax reform commission, which is scheduled to finish its work this week.

They said it looked as if the reform was not progressing as quickly or as radically as they would like. The head of the CDU in Lower Saxony state, Christian Wulff, said a cabinet reshuffle could be considered if this impression proved correct.

Kohl said a public discussion was natural when a major reform of the tax system was being considered but added: "There's no room for attempts to increase personal profiles, which just disturb our work."
